question: Which of the following metals reacts violently with cold water?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Potassium. **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Potassium metal is **soft and white with a silvery lustre, has a low melting point, and is a good conductor of heat and electricity**. 
 
• Potassium imparts a** lavender colour to a flame, and its vapour is green. **
 
• Potassium is a **silvery-white metal that is soft enough to be cut with a knife with little force. **
 
• Potassium metal reacts **r**apidly with atmospheric oxygen to form flaky white potassium peroxide in only seconds of exposure. 
 
• Potassium reacts with** cold water** **to form potassium hydroxide and hydrogen gas**

**​** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnesium** is **the eighth most abundant element in the Earth's crust, but does not occur uncombined in nature**.

 
 
• It is found in** large deposits in minerals such as magnesite and dolomite.**
 
 
 
• **Aluminum **is **a lightweight silvery white metal of main Group 13 (IIIa, or boron group) of the periodic table**.
 
 
• Aluminum is the most **abundant metallic element in Earth's crust and the most widely used nonferrous metal.**
 
 
 
• ** Zinc** is **a slightly brittle metal at room temperature and has a silvery-greyish appearance when oxidation is removed**.
 
 
• It is the **first element in group 12 (IIB) of the periodic table.**
